🇲🇽📉 <u>MEXICO HAS CUT ITS MURDER RATE IN HALF IN TWO YEARS</u>

Mexico's daily average of intentional homicides fell from 86.9 in September 2024, when Sheinbaum took office, to 43.4 in October 2026. That is a 50% drop, SESNSP head Marcela Figueroa reported at the mañanera. High-impact crimes are down 36% over the same stretch, from 636.6 a day to 409.4.

‍KJZZ: Just across the border from Arizona, Sonora has Mexico's highest 2026 dengue cases November 10, 2026 | 🟢 📰 KJZZ reports that Sonora leads Mexico with more than 2,000 dengue cases in 2026, after a wet rainy season. Arizona has 16. 🇲🇽 The figures in the article show deaths in Sonora fell from 38 last year to 5 so far this year. The headline leads with "just across the border" and the case count, not with the drop in deaths. • "Five people have died this year in Sonora" • "Thirty-eight people died from dengue by the end of the year last year"
banner: Sonora Dengue Tops Mexico, Deaths Drop

text: ‍WCJB: Columbia County man found guilty on gun charges after trying to sell, deliver guns to buyer in Mexico November 10, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Gainesville, Florida: Jose Barron, 32, pleaded guilty to agreeing to sell and deliver military-style assault weapons to a buyer in Mexico between June 2019 and February 2022. The maximum sentence is five years. 🔍 The whole story is four sentences, with no cartel framing and no follow-up on where the rifles ended up. This is the southbound side of the border story, and it ran as a short item on a local station. • "the guns were all military-style assault weapons" • "He faces up to five years in prison"
banner: Florida Man Guilty of Guns-to-Mexico Plot

text: ‍LATIN TIMES: More than 5,000 INE workers walk out across Mexico, shutting voter-ID offices November 9, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Latin Times on the INE strike: front-line workers who issue Mexico's voter IDs earn about 9,600 pesos a month, work 8am–8pm shifts and get around 12 minutes to eat. They rejected the INE's 6% raise, which works out to roughly 300 pesos a paycheck: "a mockery." 🇲🇽 The story ties the strike to Taddei's resignation over contract irregularities and notes that Sheinbaum called on the INE General Council to meet the workers' demands. • "12 minutes to eat! 12 minutes!" • "Workers organizing over poverty-level wages were being asked to wait"

‍GRIST/DRILLED: 2 years after Mexico relocated their climate-ravaged community, residents struggle to adapt November 10, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Grist and Drilled went back to El Bosque, Tabasco, the first community in Mexico officially recognized as displaced by climate change. 51 families got new homes in Nuevo Bosque, 7.5 miles inland. Two years later they've lost fishing, their diet and their community life, and the children's school is still a trailer with no bathroom. 🇲🇽 The piece credits the relocation to López Obrador's pledge and attributes the sea-level rise to fossil-fuel emissions. It quotes the residents themselves, plus a teacher, a Tabasco ecologist and a UCL law professor. • "We are grateful, but I am still grieving" • "This was supposedly a planned relocation, and yet nobody thought about education" • "No one was rich in El Bosque, but no one ever went hungry"
banner: El Bosque: Climate Exiles Still Grieving

text: ‍NYT: The Man Who Helped the C.I.A. Secretly Operate in Mexico November 10, 2026 | 🟡 📰 NYT describes a man who helped a foreign spy agency operate secretly inside Mexico, against the stated policy of Mexico's president, as a "local partner" who "quietly" built a "foothold." 🔍 The dek frames Sheinbaum's ban on US forces as a "firm line" the CIA found a way around. 🇲🇽 The CIA presence in Chihuahua is already the subject of a Mexican federal treason case against the state's former attorney general. The article is paywalled, and the headline and dek never mention Mexican law. • "drew a firm line barring U.S. forces from operating on Mexican soil" • "one local partner quietly helped the agency build a foothold"

🇲🇽💰 <u>AFORE FEES WERE CUT NEARLY IN HALF. HALF THE AFORES ALREADY OUT-EARN 2021</u>

Before the cap, Mexico's pension fund managers charged workers an average 0.98% on their balances. In 2026 it's 0.54%, the lowest since the cap began.

Even so, five of the ten afores (PensionISSSTE, Invercap, Profuturo, Inbursa and Sura) already earn more in real terms than in 2021, El Economista reports with Consar data. State-run PensionISSSTE leads: its January–September net profit is 57% above 2021.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO INE COUNCILORS: CUT YOUR OWN PAY</u>

"Let them lower their salaries, let the councilors lower them more," President Sheinbaum said at Monday's mañanera, citing the constitutional rule that no public servant may earn more than the president.

INE councilors make 262,634 pesos a month gross. At least 20,416 INE workers earn 15,856 pesos or less, and some module staff and electoral trainers get between 5,700 and 9,000.

By Monday night, INE's Blanca Cruz answered: starting in 2027, no one at the institute will earn more than the president.
banner: INE: COUNCILORS TOLD TO CUT THEIR PAY

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SUPREME COURT LETS A CASINO WALK AWAY FROM A 4.3-BILLION-PESO TAX BILL</u>

On November 9, seven justices refused to take up the case of Juegos del Bajío, a casino operator that got a 4,306-million-peso tax debt annulled in the administrative court. Hacienda documented that the company's defense rested on a forged contract. Only Lenia Batres and Irene Herrerías voted to hear it.

The majority called it res judicata because Norma Piña's old Court had already turned it down. Batres called that "a lie that should be foreign to the practices of the new Court," and noted the case was listed five times since June: "That allowed ample lobbying."
